envVars.name: XBRL_PROJECTION_APPLY
envVars.comment: screener.in is still used, for DOCUMENTS and corporate actions (stock-document-sync, corp-actions enrichment). This section used to say it ALSO writes `StockFinancials` at request time through `persistFinancialFallbackInBackground`. CORRECTED by the MONEY-1235 audit — two things were wrong:    1. THAT PATH IS DEAD IN PRACTICE. `fetchFinancialsChain` starts AND ends at      Screener since MONEY-1220 (Tickertape's rung was removed — 403 from our      egress), and `ScreenerFinancialData` carries `annualRevenue` /      `annualProfit` / `annualRoe`. It has NO `income`, `balanceSheet` or      `cashFlow` array. The three research tools read exactly those three keys      off the chain result (`fetch-income-statement.ts:198`,      `fetch-balance-sheet.ts:203`, `fetch-cash-flow.ts:184`), get `undefined`,      map zero rows, and the `if (annual.length > 0)` persist branch never      executes. The only shape that ever satisfied it was TICKERTAPE's, and      Tickertape is out of the chain. So there is no request-time SCREENER      write to `stock_financials` today.   2. It does NOT "clear `mayOverwriteFinancials` first". It CHECKS it      (`persistence.ts:291`) and `continue`s on false, counting an      `authoritySkip`. The guard is a read, not something a writer disarms.  The authority ordering the old note leaned on is correct and worth keeping, because it is what makes the dead branch SAFE rather than merely unused: FINANCIALS_AUTHORITY is NSE_XBRL > TICKERTAPE > SCREENER > YAHOO (unknown ranks LAST, so a new upstream can only fill a gap). If a future Screener parser did start emitting statement arrays and woke the branch up, it could still only land in an empty cell or over YAHOO — never over NSE_XBRL or TICKERTAPE — and the nightly projection would displace it. Left as-is by MONEY-1220 and MONEY-1235: guarded, weakest by declared authority, and as of this audit not running at all.  The screener DOCUMENTS leg is a separate question and it IS live. That "unaffected" claim rests on PROD evidence — workers stored 49 announcements, 60+ annual reports and credit ratings in the week of 2026-08-19 — NOT on a laptop 200, which is precisely the reading that hid Tickertape's block for five months. `API_LIMITS.screener` was cut 2000 -> 500 after MONEY-853, where a whole-market run hit a per-IP 429 wall and ZERO screener data reached GCS while Tickertape's leg landed normally: the same silent-partial-failure shape, from a rate limit rather than a block.  RETRACTED BY THE MONEY-1255 AUDIT. This paragraph used to say `stock-document-sync` "STILL scrapes `www.tickertape.in/stocks/<sid>`" for formatted statement text, and that `TT=0` in its job outcome would settle whether our egress is blocked on the www host. BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE, and the second one mattered: it nominated this job as a probe it can never be.  The job issues NO REQUEST to any Tickertape host. `TICKERTAPE_BASE` (`stock-document-sync-logic.ts:224` — the old note cited :202, which had moved) is read by exactly one function, `buildTickertapeUrl`, whose only two callers write the `sourceUrl` COLUMN on the upsert (`stock-document-sync.ts:565` and `:574`). The leg's actual data source is `getOrFetchFinancials`, a pure Prisma read of `stock_financials` (`packages/research/src/data-sources/db-store.ts` — "Deliberately NO external fetch here"). So `TT=250` reported 250 DATABASE LOOKUPS and `TT=0` could never occur, in any weather. `API_LIMITS.tickertape = 5000` is a per-run cap on those lookups.  Grep confirms it repo-wide: `www.tickertape.in` appears in exactly one non-test source line, the constant above. Every live Tickertape call in the repo goes to `api.tickertape.in` (the research clients), and `tickertape-client.ts:29` already records that the www host "blocks non-browser requests (404/403)" — so the citation URLs we store point at a host that would not serve us either.  MONEY-1228's Cloud Run probe is therefore still UNANSWERED and still needs to be its own measurement. What `stock-document-sync` does now report honestly is documents WRITTEN per source plus a `transportFailures` count, so a genuinely dark NSE or Screener leg is visible; before MONEY-1255 every per-source counter was incremented BEFORE the call it counted, so a source that 403s on every request still produced a full-looking number — the exact reading that hid Tickertape's block for five months, rebuilt one layer up.  Do not read "Tickertape is gone" off this section; read "Tickertape supplies neither financials nor ratios, and no job in this repo fetches from it except the research clients on `api.tickertape.in`".  Known limits, written down rather than discovered later: NSE FILERS ONLY IN THE DATA (108,020 filings, `exchange` "NSE" on every row) — but that is an UNFLIPPED SWITCH, not a missing capability, and this line said "no BSE XBRL ingest exists" for two releases while the ingest sat built and tested. MONEY-1255 shipped it DISARMED: `bse-results-xbrl` in `packages/core/src/market-data/report-registry.ts:1985` reads "WIRED BUT NOT ARMED. Arming is a founder step", alongside the BSE index path, the NBFCUploadDocument -> IFNBFCUploadDocument 404 workaround, and `resolveWritableSymbol` for BSE-only issuers that file <Symbol>NOTLISTED.  The real gate is DATA, not code: a BSE-only issuer resolves through `InstrumentMapping.bseScripCode`, and only 581 of 10,381 BSE rows carry one (330 of the 2,414 target companies). The BSE results index is keyed by scrip code and takes no date range, so without that bridge there is nothing to iterate. Realistic add: 2,414 BSE-only actives, of which ~1,643 are X/XT permitted-tier; the commercially interesting slice is ~100 A/B/T names plus ~509 SME. See MONEY-1292.  Also: history floors at 2018 (pre-2018 index records are stubs), and the 3Y/5Y CAGR columns stay null until the backfill has laid down 4 and 6 fiscal years respectively.  TWO ARM FLAGS, ONE PER JOB — MONEY-1286. `XBRL_PROJECTION_APPLY` arms the StockFinancials projection; `XBRL_RATIOS_APPLY` arms the StockRatios derivation. They were ONE flag until both gates were run against prod on 2026-08-30 and DISAGREED:    xbrlratios prod   PASS       roe READY 666/697 (95.6%), nothing BLOCKED   xbrlrecon  prod   NOT READY  totalLiabilities 17.2% disagreement,                                totalAssets/totalEquity 6.9%, netIncome 5.9%,                                against a 5.0% floor  The state the evidence supports — ratios ON, financials OFF — could not be expressed with one switch: arming what passed would have armed what failed, through a one-way door. Neither flag narrows or arms the other's job. — "true" ARMS the PROJECTION (stock_financials).

envVars.name: XBRL_RATIOS_APPLY
envVars.comment: Ships PRESENT and "false" in both cloudbuild specs — absent and "false" must not be the same state, because "absent" is exactly how MF_METADATA_PROVIDER disabled its job silently for months (MONEY-1214). Compared against the literal string, never Boolean(): Boolean("false") is true, which would arm the job in the one configuration meant to keep it off. Read PER CALL, never a module-scope const — a module-level read freezes at import, and on a warm Cloud Run container that turns a redeployed switch into no switch at all.  PRECONDITION for flipping it: the F3 reconcile (scripts/data/xbrl-reconcile.ts) reading READY. It does NOT, as of 2026-08-30 (the four disagreements above). StockFinancials has no `source` in its unique key, so the FIRST XBRL write for a period destroys the value it replaced — there is nothing left to compare against afterwards. A message may narrow this to false for one run; it can never arm one. — "true" ARMS the RATIOS job (stock_ratios). Same

envVars.name: BSE_MASTER_ENRICH
envVars.comment: MONEY-1085 — the Kite dump is NOT the whole instrument universe: it omits   NSE's SME (Emerge) and book-entry series and carries NO ISIN column, which   silently dropped ~766 NSE closing prices per trading day. NSE's own public   master CSVs (EQUITY_L.csv + SME_EQUITY_L.csv) are now a second provider   alongside Zerodha and supply both. No credentials needed.   MONEY-1205 — the Kite dump DOES quote its `name` column (106,262 of 114,427   lines; `…,SBIETFQLTY,"SBI NIFTY 200 QUALITY 30 ETF",…`). The parser split it   on `line.split(",")`, so 13,287 of 26,669 `InstrumentMapping.name` values   (49.8%, incl. 540 of 541 active ETFs) were stored WITH the literal quotes.   All three CSV parsers now share one RFC-4180 splitter   (`packages/core/src/market-data/csv-line.ts`). NSE rows looked half-healthy   only because the EQUITY_L provider's own correct splitter overwrote the   names it covers.   MONEY-1093 — the Kite dump is also NOT authoritative for `series` or   `instrumentType`: it stamps `series` from its own `instrument_type` column   ("EQ" for EVERY cash instrument, bonds included) and falls back to   instrumentType "EQUITY" for anything it cannot name-match. Because   instrument-sync runs 22:00 IST DAILY and bhavcopy-sync 21:00 IST weekdays,   it used to overwrite the real exchange series one hour after the price feed   wrote it, and revert every deliberate DEBT/REIT retype within 24h — no   error, the data just never moved. Providers now declare what they may   overwrite on an EXISTING row via `InstrumentProvider.mapToUpdate`; Zerodha   omits `series` always and `instrumentType` unless positively identified.   BSE's scrip master (api.bseindia.com ListofScripData) is a third feed   supplying the BSE group letter + ISIN for the whole ~12,600-row active   universe, so classification coverage is complete after one run instead of   accumulating over ~10 trading days. It is an UPDATE-ONLY enricher, not an   InstrumentProvider — syncInstruments upserts on symbol_exchange and BSE's   scrip_id does not always equal Kite's tradingsymbol, so a provider would   CREATE duplicates. NOTE its URL uses `segment=Debt`, which is how that   endpoint returns the FULL universe (segment=Equity gives 4,926 rows,   segment= gives 0); "fixing" it to Equity would drop every bond.   No credentials needed.    MONEY-1298 — THE REAL INDIAN CASH-EQUITY UNIVERSE IS 5,610 SYMBOLS.   Measured on prod 2026-08-30: 8,083 ISIN-bearing active rows (3,184 NSE +   4,899 BSE) collapsing to 5,610 distinct symbols and 5,615 distinct ISINs,   against 20,850 rows typed `EQUITY`. So ~61% of the "equity" table was never   equity, and three consequences all read as different bugs: ISIN coverage   reports "8,083 of 20,850" and looks like a broken enricher when it is 100%   of the real set; sector enrichment spends its weekly 500-row batch on bonds   and stamps them permanently `N/A`; and `captureRenames`   (instrument-sync.ts) filters `isin: {not: null}`, so a null-ISIN row is   excluded from rename detection and a rename orphans its price history.    The cause is the paragraph above: Kite stamps `series` "EQ" for every cash   instrument, so `classifyCashInstrument` — which reads only that column —   honestly abstained on 12,541 rows. The fix is NOT a looser series rule. It   is three MORE signals, each SUPPLIED BY THE FEED rather than inferred from   the string, and each still gated on the stamped default so a sourced value   always wins:      segment "INDICES"          213 -> INDEX  Kite naming an index outright.                                              NSE 136 + BSE 77. Ordered FIRST,                                              ahead of the ETF name matcher:                                              a fund is named after the index                                              it tracks, so the segment is the                                              only thing separating "NIFTY 50"                                              from "JIOBLACKROCK NIFTY 50 ETF".     NSE `-XX` symbol suffix  7,149 -> DEBT 6,172 · EQUITY 876 · INVIT 21 ·                                       REIT 6 · UNKNOWN 72.                                              NSE lists a non-main-board                                              instrument as <BASE>-<SERIES> and                                              `extractBaseSymbol` returns the                                              trading symbol UNCHANGED for                                              NSE/BSE — so the exchange's own                                              series is sitting in `symbol`                                              (664UP30-SG, 667GS2050-GS,                                              965SCL25C-N0). Recovered and fed                                              to the SAME tables, so a new NSE                                              debt series added to bhavcopy.ts                                              is covered automatically and the                                              EQUITY series come back EQUITY.     BSE stamped default,     no ISIN, name===symbol   5,392 -> DEBT 5,288 · ABSTAIN 104.                                              BSE's scrip master covers the                                              whole active universe in ONE run,                                              so a row it never matched is not                                              in the BSE cash-equity universe;                                              and Kite supplying the CODE as                                              the `name` is the positive signal                                              that it is a bond/CP row.    TWO RULES WERE REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT, and both would have deleted real   companies from the screener — a false DEBT verdict clears sector/industry   and the enrichment pipeline queries `instrumentType: "EQUITY"` only, so   there is no path back:     - "no ISIN -> not equity". AUGMONT ENTERPRISES is a real, newly-listed NSE       company with no ISIN yet. Absence of an ISIN is a NECESSARY GATE on       every rule above, never a sufficient signal.     - "BSE group EQ + no ISIN -> DEBT" (the shape MONEY-1302 proposed from the       30 NHAI tax-free bonds). That population also holds ~45 real companies       (TEMPSENS INSTRUMENTS, NOVYRA PHARMACHEM, BENARA BEARINGS, GLOBAL       DEFENCE INDUSTRIES), ~45 exchange-listed MF plans and ~55 BSE index       rows. Hence the `name === symbol` test.    `INDEX` is NOT a new instrumentType — it is in the schema comment,   INSTRUMENT_TYPE_MAP (Kite `IF`), quote-service's QUOTABLE_TYPES and   discover-indices. Prod holds ZERO INDEX rows today, so `getIndices` returns   an empty list; this is the one retype that ADDS a surface.    DO NOT DEACTIVATE THE 870 NSE SUFFIXED TWINS (`SYM-SM`/`-BE`/`-ST`/`-BZ`   beside a bare ISIN-bearing `SYM`). They look like duplicates worth tidying.   446 of them carry 13,917 `daily_prices` rows, 455 `latest_quotes` and 31   `stock_news` on the SUFFIXED `_id`, and `DailyPrice.instrumentId` is a   REQUIRED relation — a dangling reference THROWS and blanks every result.   Prices landed on BOTH rows (all 851 bare rows have history too). The   classifier types both EQUITY and nothing retypes them; consolidating them is   a separate ticket that has to move the price rows first. — MONEY-1093 kill-switch for the BSE scrip-master

envVars.name: FEED_ARCHIVE_MODE
envVars.comment: Raw exchange-feed archive (MONEY-1085) — prod fetches each EXCHANGE file ONCE and archives it to GCS; QA replays the same bytes through its OWN ingest instead of scraping NSE/BSE. QA keeps its own instrument _ids, so nothing in QA is ever dropped. Covered: the BSE + NSE bhavcopies, the NSE all-indices close file, the NSE instrument masters (EQUITY_L / SME_EQUITY_L) and BSE's scrip master. NOT covered: Zerodha's Kite instrument dump (api.kite.trade/instruments) fetches directly — it is an authenticated developer REST API, not a scraped exchange site, and it is public, tier-agnostic and unmetered, which is why `instrument_mappings` is QA-DIRECT in the first place. That exemption is deliberate and machine-checked by packages/core/__tests__/market-data/no-feed-fetch-bypass.test.ts (MONEY-1157).  LIVE since 2026-08-12 (MONEY-1189 / MONEY-1156): the `sync-prod-to-qa-feeds` Cloud Run job mirrors the `feeds/` prefix prod bucket -> QA bucket, so QA reads its OWN bucket and needs no prod access. Both are provisioned by scripts/ops/setup-sync-job.sh; the mirror has run and was verified at 66,951 / 66,951 object parity prod -> QA on 2026-08-13. QA then replays those bytes: FEED_ARCHIVE_MODE=replay ships in workers/cloudbuild.qa.yaml and is live on the running QA service (revision stockbook-workers-qa-00306-hmk); prod stays "archive" (workers/cloudbuild.prod.yaml).  MONEY-1194 — the job has TWO triggers, and the pair is load-bearing:   `sync-prod-to-qa-feeds-eod`   `15 21 * * 1-5` = 21:15 IST Mon-Fri   `sync-prod-to-qa-feeds-daily` `45 0 * * *`    = 00:45 IST daily The 00:45 slot alone reasoned only about the PRODUCER (prod's EOD chain) and left the mirror landing 3h45m AFTER the CONSUMER: QA runs prod's identical chain at prod's identical clock times, so QA's bhavcopy asked for day D's date-stamped object at 21:00 on day D and missed 100% (replayHits=0 replayMisses=2, measured 2026-08-13), falling back to scraping NSE + BSE every weekday — silently, because a replay miss is a soft failure by design. The ordering that must hold, all on ONE IST calendar day, is   21:00 prod ARCHIVES -> 21:15 mirror COPIES -> 21:30 QA REPLAYS, which is why `bhavcopy-sync-daily-qa` moved to 21:30. Do NOT collapse the two triggers back into one late run, and do NOT "fix" this by moving QA's bhavcopy past midnight: `resolveTargetDay` walks back to the most recent trading IST CALENDAR day, so a 01:30 run would ask for a file the exchange has not published — a silent zero-price no-op. UNDATED feeds (the instrument masters, BSE's scrip master) key under `current/`, never rotate, and were always fine.  The sequencing was load-bearing, not incidental: arming replay BEFORE the mirror exists is WORSE than leaving it off, because every key misses and silently falls back to scraping while the logs claim it replayed — so the flag was flipped in the same change that provisioned the job. That same fallback is what makes replay safe now that the mirror is real: `resolveFeedArchiveMode()` / `getFeedAsset` re-fetch from the exchange on a miss (or on an archived object that fails validation), so a late or missing mirror costs one scrape, never a failed run. — "archive" on prod, "replay" on QA — both set in

envVars.name: TIINGO_API_KEY
envVars.comment: The PAID "Connect" app (live quotes + historical candles + WebSocket ticks)   is a FOUNDER-ONLY connector in apps/web (/api/brokers/zerodha-connect) under   its OWN keys — never reuse the Personal app keys. Connecting it ONLY stores   the encrypted token for the dormant workers/src/connect code (no data sync).   ZERODHA_CONNECT_API_KEY / ZERODHA_CONNECT_API_SECRET / ZERODHA_CONNECT_REDIRECT_URI   (+ optional CONNECT_FOUNDER_EMAILS CSV; default founder deepshaswat@gmail.com) ... other brokers US price backbone — Tiingo (MONEY-980)  WHERE US PRICES COME FROM: our own `candles` warehouse, never Tiingo at request time. `CandleRepository` merges a Mongo hot window with gzipped-JSONL cold shards on GCS (`candles/{market}/{timeframe}/{symbol}/{year}`, no file extension — the format is behind the seam and is sniffed from magic bytes, so a later parquet writer reuses the same keys). India's `DailyPrice` / `IntradayBar` are untouched: MONEY-1043 is decided as COEXISTENCE.  NOTHING outside `market-data/tiingo/**`, the backfill script and `us-eod-sync` may import the Tiingo client — consumers read `CandleRepository`, so a future feed is one new `source` value plus one sync job. `api.tiingo.com`, `apimedia.tiingo.com` and `www.sec.gov` are in `FEED_HOSTS`, so a raw fetch() at any of them fails `no-feed-fetch-bypass.test.ts` by file and line.  THREE MEASURED FACTS that the code depends on and the docs get wrong:    1. The EOD CSV column order is NOT the documented one. Live header is      `date,close,high,low,open,…` — close SECOND, open FIFTH. A positional      parser written from the docs silently SWAPS open and close, producing      plausible bars and a wrong candle for every US security. Parse by header      NAME. Pinned by `tiingo-logic.test.ts`.   2. A TICKER IS NOT A SECURITY. The master holds two rows for `DOW` on NYSE      — Dow Chemical 1972-2017 and Dow Inc. 2019- — identical in exchange,      assetType and currency. 2,196 tickers repeat, 928 across venues, 834      delisted rows share a ticker with a live one. Tiingo serves only the      CURRENT occupant (asked for DOW since 1962, it returns 2019 onward), and      `permaTicker` is NOT enabled on our token. So every candle carries a      `listingId` (`{symbol}:{exchange}:{listingStartDate}`) and reads resolve      to ONE listing — a full-range read must never concatenate two companies.   3. 403 MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS. A bad token returns 403 with      `{"detail":"Invalid token."}`; an unentitled endpoint returns 403 with      ZERO bytes. 429 is undocumented and untriggered. Classify on body shape,      never on status alone.  The dedicated corporate-actions endpoints were beta-gated; BETA ACCESS IS NOW GRANTED and all five answer 200 (re-probed 2026-08-28). Leg (c) nevertheless STAYS on the derived path — dividends and splits read off the `divCash` / `splitFactor` columns that ride along on the EOD response — for a reason that only measuring revealed:    `splitStatus` DOES NOT EXIST in the live response. The docs list it ("a"   active / "c" cancelled) and it was the entire argument for switching, since   a cancelled split applied as real mis-adjusts a whole series. Measured   across 54 split rows from five ex-dates, the key union is exactly   {exDate, permaTicker, splitFactor, splitFrom, splitTo, ticker}. The endpoint   carries no cancellation signal either, so switching would buy nothing for   adjustment and cost extra requests.    `permaTicker` CANNOT replace `listingId`. It is real, and prices ARE   queryable by it, but it is absent from metadata and from the master, and   `/tiingo/daily/<permaTicker>` 404s — so it is obtainable only from a   corporate-actions row, which exists only for securities that have had one.   `DOW` and `BRKL` both return ZERO split rows, so no permaTicker exists for   the two recycled tickers the whole design was built around.  What the endpoints DO add is information not present in a price bar at all: dividend `paymentDate` / `recordDate` / `declarationDate` / `distributionFrequency`, and split `splitFrom` / `splitTo`. That is the "Dividend tracking" roadmap item as a NEW capability, tracked in MONEY-1262 — not a replacement for anything here.  Adjustment is computed at READ time (CRSP, cumulative factors back from the latest bar), so a new corporate action invalidates a cache instead of restating history — AAPL alone is 11,517 rows. Verified against Tiingo's own `adjClose` across that full series: worst error 0.023%, zero bars off by more than 0.1%.  Known limits, written down rather than discovered later: history floors at 1962; `ENE` (Enron) 404s and `LEH` (Lehman) returns an EMPTY series, so "delisted" coverage is partial and Tiingo says so ("tickers that have not yet been recycled"); the master carries CNY/HKD/AUD listings, so scope filters on `priceCurrency === "USD"` as well as exchange. Measured: 74,217 in-scope rows collapse to 72,685 primary listings — 15,629 equities, 7,642 ETFs and 49,414 mutual funds (41,371 active / 31,314 delisted) AS OF THAT MEASUREMENT. Re- measured 2026-08-30 the master holds 74,134 rows — 41,352 active / 32,782 delisted (MF 27,289/22,557, Stock 8,307/8,100, ETF 5,756/2,125). The universe GREW; neither figure is wrong, so both carry their date rather than one quietly overwriting the other.  THE permaTicker ENRICHER IS ACTIVE-ONLY BY DESIGN, so a DELISTED listing never gets one. A documented coverage FLOOR, not a bug and not a backlog that converges. `permaTicker` has exactly one writer, `enrichUsInstrumentsWithPermaTicker`, whose page is `where: { listingStatus: "ACTIVE" }` (`tiingo-search.ts:197`/`:211`), and the filter cannot simply be widened: Tiingo's search resolves the CURRENT occupant of a ticker, so a delisted predecessor would be handed its SUCCESSOR's permaTicker — another company's dividends and splits on our join key, silently, which is finding 2 above from the other side. Measured 2026-08-30:    22,556 delisted mutual funds    8,100 delisted stocks    2,125 delisted ETFs  What that costs differs by asset class, and the difference is the whole point of having TWO keys. `Candle` keys on `listingId` (`{symbol}:{exchange}:{listingStartDate}`), which is derivable from the master for every row — so the 8,100 stocks and 2,125 ETFs ARE reachable, through the BACKFILL (`scripts/jobs/tiingo-us-backfill.ts --only-delisted`), just never through the nightly legs, which narrow to ACTIVE in `buildUsEodWhere`. `UsFundNav` keys on `(permaTicker, date)`, which is NOT derivable — so the 22,556 delisted funds will NEVER receive a NAV row, from the nightly job or the backfill (it checkpoints them `NO_PERMATICKER` and moves on). Subject to `LEH`-style upstream gaps on top of that.  So do not read a low `us_fund_nav` coverage ratio against the whole 49,846-fund master as a defect: the reachable denominator is the ACTIVE partition, and the nightly job no longer spends a billed request discovering that per fund (MONEY-1291 — it skips before the fetch, not after).  MUTUAL FUNDS ARE IN SCOPE, on the NMFQS venue, and that is load-bearing rather than generous: the nightly job has a NAV leg, and a leg whose population is empty by construction selects nothing, writes nothing and reports HEALTHY forever. A fund's OHLC fields carry its NAV.  SCHEDULING FOLLOWS THE US CLOCK, not ours. Fund NAVs publish after 12:00 AM ET = 10:30 IST under EST, which is LATER than the 8:00 PM ET equity correction window (06:30 IST). The nightly job therefore runs 11:00 IST, gated by the later of the two boundaries — an earlier run fetches an empty NAV set every night without failing. Crons are Tue-Sat IST because a US session closes 4:00 PM ET, which lands after midnight IST the following day.    10:00 IST  us-instrument-master-sync   prod   11:00 IST  us-eod-sync                 prod  (PROD_ONLY)   14:00 IST  us-instrument-master-sync   qa  QA DOES NOT RUN THE PRICE JOB, and that differs from India on purpose. `bhavcopy-sync` runs in BOTH envs replaying prod's archived bytes, because `DailyPrice` keys on `instrumentId` and QA holds its own instrument _ids — the rows are not portable, so QA has to re-INGEST rather than receive. `Candle` deliberately keys on (symbol, exchange, timeframe, ts) and carries NO ObjectId reference, so it IS portable: `us-eod-sync-daily` is in PROD_ONLY_JOBS and `candles` + `fx_rates` are in REFERENCE_COLLECTIONS, so QA receives exactly what prod computed.  That is strictly safer than the replay arrangement here, because Tiingo is a PAID METERED api and a replay MISS is a soft failure by design: any drift in the mirror timing would silently spend a second full copy of the quota (~73k requests) instead of degrading. Copying rows removes that failure mode rather than scheduling around it.  The MASTER still runs in both envs, because `instrument_mappings` is QA-DIRECT and cannot be synced down. That costs nothing: `supported_tickers.zip` is a PUBLIC file (verified 200 with no Authorization header) archived UNDATED under `current/`, so it never races a mirror and spends no quota. — GCP Secret Manager: TIINGO_API_KEY_QA / _PROD.

envVars.name: DATABENTO_API_KEY
envVars.comment: US INTRADAY — Databento (MONEY-1373)  TWO SOURCES, TWO JOBS, AND THE SPLIT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Databento is the source of BACKTEST-GRADE truth: consolidated, trade-derived, real volume. Tiingo stays the source of everything a USER sees. Nothing here touches India (`DailyPrice` / `IntradayBar` — MONEY-1043 is decided as COEXISTENCE) or Tiingo's daily EOD candles.  WHAT WE ACTUALLY BUY, and it is not the consolidated tape. `EQUS.MINI` is a single ANONYMIZED consolidated publisher (`EQUS.MINI.EQUS`, publisher id 95). Its bars are TRADE-derived and carry REAL volume — which is the property the realtime feed cannot provide at all — but it is a VENUE BLEND, a subset of the SIP rather than the SIP itself. Do not describe it as "the tape"; a backtest sized against it is sized against a subset, and the difference is exactly the kind of thing that never shows up as an error.  HISTORY FLOORS AT 2023-03-28. Not eight years, not "since inception" — that is where EQUS.MINI begins, and it is enforced in the manifest's Zod schema (`historyFloor >= EQUS_MINI_HISTORY_FLOOR`) rather than left to the operator. Asking for a session before it returns an EMPTY result, which is indistinguishable from a market holiday and from a broken query.  ── THE ONE-SOURCE RULE, AND WHY THE KEY IS AN ET SESSION DATE ──────────────  A `(symbol, timeframe, session)` holds bars from exactly ONE `source`. That rule predates Databento (MONEY-1309, `mayWriteIntoDay`) and is deliberately named after the PROPERTY rather than after a vendor: a quote-derived bar beside a trade-derived one puts a structural `volume: 0` next to a real volume and changes what OHLC MEANS partway through a day, with nothing on the rows to reveal it.  THE KEY IS THE ET SESSION DATE, NOT THE UTC DAY, and that changed with this ticket. The US session runs 04:00–20:00 ET. Under EST the post-market runs to 20:00 ET, which is the NEXT UTC day — and also the UTC day of the FOLLOWING session's pre-market. So a UTC key spans the tail of one session and the head of the next, and whichever writer lands there first locks the other out of BOTH. `usMarketDateKey` is the key; `groupRowsBySession` and `RtCandleSink.resolveDayVerdicts` both use it.  DISPLACEMENT IS ONE-WAY. Databento REPLACES a `TIINGO_RT` session wholesale (delete, then write — in that order, so a crash leaves a gap rather than a mixture). The reverse is REFUSED. `D1` is NEVER displaced by anything, and the timeframe guard is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: a mutation test removing it proved the authority ranks ALONE do not refuse a daily displacement. The counter `databento.displaced_d1` must read ZERO forever — the manifest's schema enum cannot even express a daily entry, so a non-zero value means a writer path exists that no manifest can produce.  PRICE-SOURCE AUTHORITY: BHAVCOPY 100 > TIINGO 60 > DATABENTO 55 > ZERODHA 50 > TIINGO_RT 20 > YAHOO 10 > unknown 1. Read the two US ranks together: DATABENTO below TIINGO because Tiingo's DAILY bar is the adjusted, corporate-action-aware series the app renders and Databento's is raw intraday; DATABENTO far above TIINGO_RT because one is trade-derived with real volume and the other is a mid-price with a structural zero.  TIMEFRAME LITERALS ARE `M1` / `H1` / `S1`. Never `"1m"`. The repo's timeframe vocabulary is `D1` / `M1` / `M5` / `M15` / `H1` / `W1`; the vendor's SCHEMA names (`ohlcv-1m`) are converted at exactly one place, `SCHEMA_TIMEFRAME`.  ── THE ARCHIVE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  Raw vendor bytes land at `databento/{dataset}/{schema}/{year}/{jobId}/`, DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE `feeds/`: the prod->QA mirror rsyncs that whole prefix twice daily and this data is bought, not scraped. Lifecycle is Nearline at 30 days and NEVER a Delete — these bytes are the only copy of something bought once, and deleting them turns a re-load into a re-purchase of a $199 Standard month. `databento/` is on BOTH `ALLOW_PREFIXES` and `PROTECTED_ROOTS` in `setup-gcs-lifecycle.sh`, and a test fails on a Delete rule under it.  CSV + ZSTD, NOT DBN. Databento's native format is DBN and there is no TypeScript decoder for it. The server-side transcode to CSV is FREE and billing is on the BINARY size either way, so the choice costs nothing and removes a dependency we would have had to write. `pretty_px`, `pretty_ts` and `map_symbols` are all on, so prices arrive as decimals and rows carry the symbol.  WHICH IS WHY THE WORKERS IMAGE IS NODE 22. `zlib.createZstdDecompress` landed in Node 22.15; on 20 there is no stdlib zstd and the alternative is a native addon in an alpine/musl image. The bump was verified by REQUIRING the module inside the built image, not by trusting the changelog.  OHLCV-1s IS ARCHIVE-ONLY, by founder decision. It is the TB-scale entry and it is LAST in the manifest's submit order. Nothing loads it into `candles`; a future backtest reads it from the archive. `--apply` without `--entry=` exits 1 for exactly this reason — a bare apply would reach it in the same 24-hour execution as everything else.  ── THE MONEY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  `cost_usd` IS NULL AT SUBMISSION. It only appears once the vendor has processed the job, so a budget guard reading it at submit time would sum to zero — and a budget that reads zero authorises everything. Every purchase is therefore QUOTED first through `metadata.get_cost` (free, and it "respects any discounts provided by flat rate plans", so a window included in the Standard subscription quotes $0.00 — which is how the runbook confirms the subscription is live before spending anything).  THE LEDGER REFUSES, IT NEVER TRIMS. A submission that would cross `DATABENTO_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD` throws. Narrowing the window to fit would buy a slice nobody asked for and report success, which is the failure shape this whole ticket is built around. Every `submitBatchJob(` call site is inside `withDatabentoBudget(`, enforced by a SOURCE SCAN — MONEY-1309 is why it is a scan and not a review note: a guard wired at one of five legs under-reported spend by ~80%, which is worse than no guard because it manufactures headroom.  A WINDOW IS NEVER BOUGHT TWICE, and that is now a database constraint: `DatabentoBatchJob` is `@@unique([purpose, entryId, schema, symbolsHash, start, end])`. `jobId` is OPTIONAL and only `@@index`ed — the guard creates the row in `QUOTED` BEFORE submitting, so a crash between the two leaves a visible row rather than spend nobody can find; and MongoDB's unique indexes are not sparse, so a unique over an optional `jobId` would admit exactly ONE un-submitted row in the whole collection.  FILES EXPIRE 30 DAYS AFTER SUBMISSION — not after completion, which is the reading that leaves a job less time than it appears to have. Past it the only remedy is to buy the range again, at usage prices, after the subscription has lapsed. Rows within two days are reported at ERROR level with a counter.  ── THE TWO JOBS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────    databento-harvest   ONE-TIME, one manifest entry per execution, run by hand                       from the runbook. NO scheduler trigger at all — a cron                       would be a standing authorisation to spend against a                       subscription meant to be cancelled once the harvest                       completes. 24 h task timeout, 4Gi.   databento-append    NIGHTLY, PROD_ONLY. 2 h task timeout, 2Gi.  THE APPEND RUNS 15:00 IST AND 18:00 IST, TUE–SAT. Not 13:00: the vendor's T+1 embargo releases the prior session at roughly 09:00 UTC = 14:30 IST, so a 13:00 cron would ask for a session that does not exist and get an empty result that reads as a quiet market. Tue–Sat because a US session closing 16:00 ET lands after midnight IST on the following day. The cron is the CHEAP half of that guard; the job also reads `metadata.get_dataset_range` before computing a gap, so a late vendor produces a named `NOT_YET_PUBLISHED` skip. The three skip reasons (`NO_HWM_RUN_HARVEST_FIRST`, `UP_TO_DATE`, `NOT_YET_PUBLISHED`) are DISTINCT values: collapsing them would make a never-harvested entry report the same thing, forever, as a perfectly current one.  QA RECEIVES ROWS, NOT BYTES. Databento is a paid metered vendor and QA never spends there. `candles`, `databento_batch_jobs`, `us_cost_model_versions` and `us_cost_model_rows` are in `sync-prod-to-qa.sh`'s REFERENCE_COLLECTIONS, so QA gets exactly what prod computed — the same arrangement as `us-eod-sync`, and strictly safer than the feeds REPLAY arrangement, where a mirror miss silently re-spends the quota instead of degrading.  ── THE TRANSACTION-COST MODEL ─────────────────────────────────────────────  Built MONTHLY from the archived `bbo-1m` quotes, into `us_cost_model_rows`: one median and 75th-percentile spread per (listing, time-of-day bucket), plus a liquidity tier. Reads are VERSION-PINNED — a backtest run against March's spreads and re-run in September against September's produces two different P&Ls from identical inputs, with nothing in either result to say why. The version bumps in ONE place, the append's monthly trigger.  The field names in `packages/types/src/us-cost-model.ts` ARE the Mongo field names, because the quant engine is PYTHON and reads the collections directly: a rename that "only changes TypeScript" breaks a consumer no TypeScript build can see. — SECRET. envVars.comment: US fundamentals — SEC EDGAR (MONEY-979), services/us-fundamentals  A PYTHON Cloud Run service, because the parser is Python: edgartools maps 2,923 XBRL tags onto ~95 standard concepts and parses Forms 3/4/5, 13F, 13D/G and 8-K exhibits. It lives in `services/` rather than `apps/*` or `packages/*` because those two are literal Yarn WORKSPACE GLOBS — a directory there needs a package.json or `yarn install`, Turbo's task graph and gen-test-coverage.ts all break on it. `services/` is language-neutral and top-level, the same shape `workers` has; a future Rust service goes in the same place. Docker is the deployment boundary, not Turbo. The seam to the TS side is Mongo + Pub/Sub, never an import, and a test enforces that.  ONLY PROD FETCHES FROM SEC. Cloud Run has shared egress IPs and SEC's fair-access limit is PER IP, so two environments scraping one budget is two environments getting blocked. QA runs SEC_EGRESS=off — every client method raises before opening a socket — and receives rows through sync-prod-to-qa.  THE LIMITER IS OURS, NOT THE LIBRARY'S. edgartools' own docs claim "distributed rate limiting"; the source does not have it. `httpclient.py:205` builds a per-process `InMemoryBucket` from EDGAR_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC. N instances x 9 req/s is exactly how an IP gets blocked, so we assign a pyrate_limiter RedisBucket to `edgar.httpclient.HTTP_MGR.rate_limiter` (it is looked up at CALL time; no module captures it) and share ONE bucket across every instance and job. It FAILS CLOSED: Redis unreachable stops the run rather than silently reverting to per-process 9/s, because that fallback is invisible until the block arrives. The library also NEVER retries 429 and never sleeps on Retry-After — and SEC sends neither, signalling a block with a 403 and a BODY ("Undeclared Automated Tool"), so classification is on body text, never on status. — The User-Agent, sent VERBATIM and unvalidated by

envVars.comment: "statsd" on the SERVICE. Not a preference — a property of where the process runs. The service has a `datadog-agent` sidecar listening on UDP 8125; the JOBS have NO sidecar, so every counter they emitted was refused by a closed port and dropped, silently, while `[job-outcome] {...}` logged perfectly. DogStatsD is fire-and-forget, so nothing failed and the metric simply never arrived — which renders as NO DATA, not as an alert, and is indistinguishable from an idle healthy job. On "http" the outcome POSTs to api.us5.datadoghq.com/api/v1/series and needs DD_API_KEY (also newly mounted on the jobs); without the key it NO-OPS, matching `datadog-metrics` on the TypeScript side. Compared to the LITERAL string: bool("statsd") is true, so a coercion would put the SERVICE on HTTP and have it bypass its own healthy sidecar. Both specs ship it PRESENT (MONEY-1214). — /tmp/edgar. edgartools mkdirs its data dir AT

envVars.name: EDGAR_DETECT
envVars.comment: IMPORT and writes an HTTP cache there; Cloud Run's filesystem is read-only except /tmp. — "on" arms the minutely getcurrent walk.

envVars.name: EDGAR_PARSE_APPLY
envVars.comment: SHIPS ARMED ON PROD ("on"), off on QA. — "true" arms the five parsers' writes.

envVars.name: EDGAR_EVICT_APPLY
envVars.comment: SHIPS ARMED ON PROD ("true"), off on QA. — "true" arms the 13F evictor's DELETES.

envVars.name: OPENFIGI_API_KEY
envVars.comment: OFF IN BOTH — the one exception, and not out of caution. The 13F cold tier it evicts into is registered at boot but UNREACHABLE: `getManagerHoldings` is its only reader and has zero callers, so eviction would delete readable rows and then answer "not yet ingested" for periods whose shards sit unread in GCS. Harmless on day one, wrong a quarter later. Arm it once a manager-side tool consumes the cold tier — docs/reference/edgar-engine.md section 11.  The INGEST PATH SHIPS RUNNING, the way the Tiingo US backbone shipped (MONEY-980: live schedules, no apply flag at all). A feature behind an off switch is a feature that does not exist — nothing exercises its write path and the monitors have no series to watch.  QA is off because it has NO SEC EGRESS (SEC_EGRESS=off; the fair-access limit is PER IP and Cloud Run shares egress addresses). An armed detector there would raise on all 1,440 runs a day. Forced, not chosen.  All three are still PRESENT in both specs. Absent and explicitly-set must not be the same state — that is how MF_METADATA_PROVIDER disabled its job silently for months (MONEY-1214). Compared to the LITERAL string, never Boolean(): Boolean("false") is true. `INTENDED_FLAG_STATE` in tests/test_deploy_contract.py pins BOTH directions, so a silent disarm fails too. — GCP Secret Manager: OPENFIGI_API_KEY_QA / _PROD.
